newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: TROPICAL CYCLONE RACHEL IN TOP-END
In Australia's top-end, newly named Tropical Cyclone Rachel is threatening communities from Croker Island to Port Keats, including Darwin.
The Northern Territory weather bureau says the cyclone's currently off the coast, and wind and rain is continuing to lash island and coastal communities.
Wild storms in Darwin overnight brought down trees and power lines, and caused widespread flooding.
In the Tiwi Islands close to the centre of the low pressure system some residents moved into cyclone shelters in the early hours of this morning.
Police Sergeant Shane Taylor who's based on Melville Island north of Darwin says weather conditions have varied with heavy rain, and strong wind gusts in some areas.
AMA CALLS FOR REMOVAL OF LOGOS ON CRICKET BATS
The Australian Medical Association is calling for the Pakistan Cricket team to remove the cigarette advertising carried on its bats before today's match against the West Indies in Brisbane.
The A-M-A also wants an explanation from the Federal Opposition following comments on the issue yesterday by its acting health spokesman, Daryl Melham.
Mr Melham is reported to have described the controversy as an over-reaction because the cigarette brand in question is not sold in Australia.
A-M-A Federal President, Dr Keith Woollard says Australia has a moral obligation to set an example for the developing world, where tobacco control is either in its infancy or non-existent.
NORTHS INVESTIGATING CAPTAIN'S CRICKET PERFORMANCE
The North Sydney rugby league club is investigating reports that team captain, Jason Taylor was one of several first-grade players escorted from the S-C-G on Wednesday.
The group was watching the one-day cricket match between Australia and Pakistan, and were ordered to leave following complaints about their behaviour.
Norths' chief executive, Bob Saunders, says from information he's received so far Taylor didn't do anything wrong except stand on a chair.
But he says the matter's being investigated and if anything out of order did happened, Taylor will be dealt with appropriately.
NO MORE CHEAP DRUGS FOR VISITORS
In a bid to save six million dollars a year on the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme, foreign visitors to Australian will no longer be able to get cheap pharmaceutical drugs.
In the past tourists and temporary overseas visitors were able to buy subsidised drugs under the Scheme.
But the Health Department says the subsidies will now only be available to people who can prove Australian residency, and people from countries with reciprocal health care agreements.
The Department of Health's Dr David Graham says the changes aim to ensure the scheme remains efficient and cost effeective.
